# UN Human Rights Database (UNHRDB)

> Paragraph-level research database of UN human rights law, built at Adam Mickiewicz University, Poznań (Łukasz Szoszkiewicz, Zuzanna Kowalska). It holds 6,152 UN documents split into 326,448 numbered paragraphs, each keyed to its UN document symbol and paragraph number, so a passage can be quoted and cited exactly. Free to use; open source.

## What is in it

- Treaty Body General Comments and General Recommendations: 188 documents, 7,304 paragraphs, all ten UN treaty bodies, 1972–2026.
- Individual-communication decisions (views, admissibility decisions) of 8 treaty bodies: 4,333 decisions, 152,731 paragraphs, 1977–2025.
- Thematic reports of the UN Special Procedures: 1,631 reports from all 46 thematic mandates, 166,413 paragraphs, 1960–2026. Country-visit reports, communications and addenda are out of scope.
- Recommendations to States (concluding observations, Universal Periodic Review and Special Procedures recommendations) from OHCHR's Universal Human Rights Index, served live.

Texts are the UN's own wording. Footnotes, section headings and paragraph numbering follow the published documents; Special Procedures texts come from the Word files on UN Documents where one exists (1,550 of 1,631 reports), otherwise from the PDF.

## Legal character

General Comments are authoritative interpretations of a treaty by its monitoring body. Treaty-body decisions apply a treaty to an individual case. Special Procedures reports are the independent opinion of a mandate-holder (soft law). Keep the three apart when stating what the law requires.

## How to link and cite

- A paragraph: https://lszoszk.github.io/generalcomments/?p=<paragraph-id>, e.g. https://lszoszk.github.io/generalcomments/?p=ccpr-c-gc-36-0012 (Human Rights Committee, general comment No. 36, para. 12).
- A search: https://lszoszk.github.io/generalcomments/?q=<terms> (operators and filters below).
- Every document as a plain HTML page without JavaScript, full text with paragraph anchors: https://lszoszk.github.io/generalcomments/d/<document-id>/#p<paragraph>, e.g. https://lszoszk.github.io/generalcomments/d/ccpr-c-gc-36/#p12. Index of all documents: https://lszoszk.github.io/generalcomments/d/
- Cite the underlying UN document by its symbol and paragraph (e.g. CCPR/C/GC/36, para. 12); the official text is at https://docs.un.org/en/<symbol>.
- Cite the database itself as: Szoszkiewicz, Ł., & Kowalska, Z. (2026). UNHRDB — UN Human Rights Database (Version 2.2.0). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10495719

## Search syntax and filter URLs

Query operators (parameter q):
- "exact phrase" — the words verbatim and in order; no stemming.
- A B — whitespace is AND: both terms must appear.
- A AND B, A OR B — AND binds tighter than OR; group with ( … ).
- A NOT B, or A -B — exclude B; an exclusion needs a positive term beside it.
- prefix* — trailing asterisk matches any continuation (discriminat* finds discrimination, discriminatory).
- Bare words match the word form as typed; there is no proximity (NEAR) operator.

Filters, each a URL parameter; several values are joined with | :
- scope — gc (General Comments, the default), jur (treaty-body decisions), sp (Special Procedures reports), all (the three together), rec (recommendations to States).
- tb — treaty body or mandate, as shown in the filter panel: CCPR, CESCR, CRC, CEDAW, CERD, CAT, CRPD, CMW, CED; Special Procedures as "SR Privacy", "SR Torture", "WG Arbitrary Detention" and so on.
- y1, y2 — first and last year.
- g — groups concerned, e.g. Children, Women/girls, Persons with disabilities, Indigenous peoples, Migrants.
- jur only: cy (State party, e.g. Algeria), oc (outcome: violation_found, merits_no_violation, inadmissible, discontinued).
- fn=1 also searches footnotes (off by default).

Examples:
- https://lszoszk.github.io/generalcomments/?q=%22best+interests%22+-adoption&tb=CRC|CESCR&g=Children
- https://lszoszk.github.io/generalcomments/?q=%22enforced+disappearance%22&scope=jur&tb=CCPR&cy=Algeria&oc=violation_found&y1=2015
- https://lszoszk.github.io/generalcomments/?q=biometric*+AND+(surveillance+OR+facial)&scope=sp&y1=2018

## Using it from an AI assistant

- Connector (MCP, Streamable HTTP, no key): https://150.254.115.204/unhrdb-mcp-rpc/mcp — tools search_paragraphs, lookup_by_citation, search_recommendations, lookup_recommendation, list_uhri_facets.
- Claude plugin with the connector and three skills (un-human-rights-research, un-citation-check, treaty-body-case-law): https://github.com/lszoszk/mcp-unhrdb#skills-for-claude. Skills for the recommendations to States (uhri-plus, uhri-plus-country-brief, uhri-plus-legal-grounding, uhri-plus-dashboard-link): https://lszoszk.github.io/UnitedNations_recommendations/skills/README.md. In Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add lszoszk/mcp-unhrdb`, then `/plugin install unhrdb@mcp-unhrdb`.
- Step-by-step guide to connecting Claude, ChatGPT and other assistants: https://lszoszk.github.io/UnitedNations_recommendations/ai.html
- Quote the returned text verbatim and cite the UN symbol and paragraph. Searches require all bare words (use OR, "phrases" and prefix*); check that a looked-up paragraph carries the label you asked for.
